$comment: The film registry. scripts/lib/films.mjs checks it and writes every film's pages (web/f/<slug>/) and the home page from web/templates/; scripts/contract.mjs expands contract.yaml's films block from it. A live film is served and checked in full. A film in production (status in_production) is listed on the home page by title, dates and status only: no page, no media, no synopsis. A paused film is taken off this file. A caption track is offered only once its review is 'reviewed'. screenplay_path (optional): where the film's working screenplay lives on the render machine (~ is the home folder), so the engine's bed-reuse lint (GRAMMAR A29 refined) can refuse a score another film already plays; DOCUMENT_FILMS overrides it. balance_fallback: only the Partition pilot, whose live sources.json predates the balance block, may show its own figures without declaring one.

films.title: Not a Free Agent
films.logline: the line, the roads, and the women both governments set out to recover
films.synopsis: In December 1947 the governments of India and Pakistan agreed to recover the women abducted in the violence of Partition, and recorded that the women's own wishes were irrelevant. A narrator follows the record from Noakhali in 1946 to the agreement of April 1950: the conferences, the camps, the ordinance and the December 1949 debate, in the words of the members who argued it, women among them.
films.content_note: It tells of killing, abduction and flight.
films.shows: This film shows no bodies or killing.

related.name: The Partition of India, in sound
related.line: Listen to void history's audio documentary on the Partition of India
related.where: On void history, part of the void family.

films.title: The Next Village
films.logline: a goddess, a needle, and a search from house to house
films.synopsis: In the villages of Bihar the disease was called by the goddess's name: Sitala. Among the Yoruba it belonged to the god of the earth. From 1966, searchers went from house to house and from village to village to find every case of smallpox. A narrator tells it in the words of the time, with readings from the record: the goddess and the god, the ring around each case, the farewell in Bihar, the last known cases, and the two years of looking that followed.
films.content_note: It shows people ill with smallpox, children among them.
films.shows: This film shows people with smallpox in photographs and medical films of the time.

films.title: Real World
films.logline: one day, as it was heard by the people working the sky and the city below
films.synopsis: On 11 September 2001, controllers at Boston and New York and the air defence sector tried to understand what was happening in the air. The film keeps to what was known that day, hour by hour: the tapes of the control rooms and the defence sector in the morning, and what was said and reported in public as the day went on. A narrator gives the time, the place and what was reported; the recordings carry the rest.
films.content_note: It concerns the attacks of 11 September 2001. It plays air traffic and air defence recordings made that day.
films.shows: This film shows the day as it was broadcast and photographed: the burning towers, the second impact, the Pentagon security camera's view of the impact, and the dust after the collapses, in wide views. It never shows an identifiable person in their final moments; a wide view is never zoomed in, slowed or held on a person; no final call is played; the dead are shown by what the day left empty.

films.title: Market Street
films.logline: a cable car ride down one street, and the same corners in May
films.synopsis: In the spring of 1906 the Miles brothers put a camera on the front of a cable car and filmed Market Street, San Francisco, from the moving car, east toward the Ferry Building. The film plays the ride, then follows the record from Tuesday 17 April, when Caruso sang Carmen and went back to the Palace Hotel on Market Street, through the days of the fire: the troops on Market Street that morning, the mayor's proclamation, the fire at Third by noon and at Van Ness on Thursday night. The witnesses are quoted from their printed accounts: Funston in Cosmopolitan, Jack London in Collier's, Caruso in The Theatre. In May a Biograph camera films at Eighth and Market, where trolley wire has been strung over the cable line. Then the ride resumes, to the end of the line.
films.content_note: It tells of an earthquake and the fire that followed, and of soldiers posted with orders to shoot looters, and of looters shot. The dead are counted in a newspaper of the time; the later counts are on the Sources page.
films.shows: This film shows the street and the people on it in the spring of 1906, the fire from Sacramento Street on the morning of 18 April, the crowds at the foot of Market Street and the ruins, in photographs of the time. The days of the fire are seen in photographs and printed pages; the moving pictures are from before and from May. It shows no bodies and no one hurt. A front page of 19 April, read on screen, gives its own estimate of the dead; the later counts are on the Sources page.

films.title: Endurance
films.logline: twenty-eight men, a ship held in the ice, and the days counted from South Georgia
films.synopsis: In December 1914 the Endurance enters the pack ice of the Weddell Sea with Ernest Shackleton and twenty-seven men who mean to cross the continent on foot. The ice holds her from January 1915. In October it crushes her, and the men camp on the floe, three hundred and forty-six miles from the nearest land they know of, with two pounds of personal gear each. The floe carries them north past land they cannot reach, until it splits under the camp on 9 April 1916 and the boats are launched for Elephant Island. Six men sail the decked boat eight hundred miles for South Georgia; twenty-two wait under two upturned boats, and the film waits with them. The record is Frank Hurley's photographs and colour plates, the diaries read with their dates, and a recording of Shackleton's voice from 1910. It ends on 30 August 1916.
films.content_note: It tells of a ship crushed by ice, of dogs and a cat shot, and of an amputation.
films.shows: This film shows the ship held, heeled and crushed in Hurley's photographs, the camps on the floe and the men under the boats on Elephant Island, and the pages of McNish's journal. It shows no bodies, no wounds and no animal killed: the shooting of the dogs and the operation on Blackborow's toes are in words only. There is no photograph of the boat journey, the crossing of South Georgia or the rescue; they are told over the expedition's maps and the diarists' words.

films.title: Houston, We've Had a Problem
films.logline: four days in April 1970, as they were heard on the loops between the spacecraft and the room in Houston
films.synopsis: On the evening of 13 April 1970, fifty-five hours into the flight, the crew of Apollo 13 end a television tour of their lunar module with a good night. Minutes later they report a problem. The film keeps to the recordings made during the flight, the air-to-ground loop and the flight director's loop, with NASA's photographs of the control room, the crew's own film and frames, and pages of the 1970 transcription: the handover to Glynn Lunney's team, the burns, the pass behind the Moon, the canister built from what was aboard, the cold, the service module seen with one side gone, the entry, and the recovery ship on 17 April. A narrator gives the time and what was decided; the loops carry the rest.
films.content_note: It concerns a failure aboard a spacecraft with three men far from Earth, and their return. It plays the air-to-ground and control room recordings made during the flight.
films.shows: This film shows the control room in NASA's photographs, the crew in the lunar module on their own 16 mm film and in their own frames, the far side of the Moon as they photographed it, the service module after it was cast off, and pages of the 1970 transcription. There is no film of the control room in it: the room is seen in photographs. No one in it is hurt. It ends on 17 April 1970 and does not say what caused the failure.
